Research

Computational astrophysics · Numerical methods · Disk dynamics

Planet–disk interactions and transition disks

I am working with FARGO3D to investigate gas and dust dynamics in protoplanetary disks, including planet-driven gaps and ring structures. The work combines numerical simulation, high-performance computing, and Python-based analysis.

  • Running and comparing hydrodynamic simulations on university high-performance computing resources.
  • Analyzing gas and dust surface-density structures, velocity fields, and planet locations.
  • Developing reusable plotting and post-processing tools to compare simulation runs and quantify disk features.

Research status: Ongoing computational project. Detailed results, figures, and publications can be added as they become ready to share.

Projects

Formula SAE vehicle simulation

Developing a MATLAB-based multibody lap simulation for a Formula SAE vehicle. The project brings together vehicle dynamics, tire behavior, powertrain constraints, and track-event modeling.

  • Modeling acceleration, skidpad, and endurance events.
  • Exploring suspension geometry, tire cornering behavior, and vehicle inertial properties.
  • Investigating opportunities to incorporate lightweight machine-learning features into engineering workflows.

Scientific computing and data analysis

Building Python tools for simulation data inspection, visualization, and comparison. Current interests include reproducible computational workflows, numerical analysis, and translating model outputs into interpretable results.

Project descriptions are intentionally concise; add repository links, selected figures, and technical write-ups as each project is ready for public presentation.
